questions.q: What does a storage event trigger fire in response to?
options: A real event on a storage account, like a blob being created or deleted
A wall-clock schedule
A periodic time interval with retained state
Only a manual on-demand run
questions.explain: Storage event triggers are event-driven, firing when a matching blob is created or deleted, via Azure Event Grid — no schedule involved at all.

questions.q: What pattern-matching options does a storage event trigger support?
options: Blob path begins with and Blob path ends with — no other wildcards
Full regular expressions on the blob path
Only exact file name matches, with no path matching at all
SQL-style LIKE patterns
questions.explain: These two properties are the only pattern matching a storage event trigger supports, and at least one of them is required.

questions.q: How does a triggered pipeline actually learn which file arrived?
options: The trigger captures it as @triggerBody().folderPath and @triggerBody().fileName, mappable to pipeline parameters
The pipeline must poll the storage account itself to find out
It's impossible to know which file triggered the run
Only the file's size is passed, never its name or path
questions.explain: Mapping these trigger properties to pipeline parameters during setup lets any activity reference the arrived file's exact path and name.

questions.q: Does Data Factory poll the storage account directly to detect a new file?
options: No — it subscribes to Azure Event Grid, which pushes the event the moment storage reports it
Yes, it polls the storage account continuously
Yes, but only once per hour
It requires a self-hosted integration runtime to detect events
questions.explain: This is a push model via Event Grid, not a polling loop — Data Factory makes no direct contact with the storage account just to detect the event itself.

questions.q: What storage account types currently support storage event triggers?
options: Azure Data Lake Storage Gen2 and general-purpose v2 storage accounts
Any storage account type, with no restrictions
Only Azure SQL Database
Only Azure Table Storage
questions.explain: Storage event triggers currently support ADLS Gen2 and general-purpose v2 accounts specifically, built on the underlying Event Grid integration.
